en: Temperature measures the average energy of motion of particles, so a hot drink has faster-moving particles than a cold one.
Diffusion happens fastest in gases, slower in liquids, and slowest in solids because of differences in particle spacing and motion.
A gas spreads out to fill its entire container because its particles move freely in every direction with almost no forces between them.
Hot water dissolves sugar faster than cold water because its particles move faster and bump into the sugar more often.
Water vapor is invisible; the white mist above boiling water is actually tiny liquid droplets, not the gas itself.
Liquid particles pull on each other, creating a surface film that lets small insects walk on water.
Under a microscope, tiny pollen grains in water jiggle randomly because invisible water particles bump into them, showing the particle model.
Sublimation and deposition are opposite changes: sublimation turns solid to gas, and deposition turns gas to solid, both skipping the liquid state.
